hypotheses.claim: A single-order-vectorized blend of farness (mean distance from candidate to remaining unvisited cities) with a small destination-pull term (d(0,u)) and a nearest-neighbor distance term, restricted to the K nearest candidates, retains most of T46's farness quality (+14.3% gap class) while cutting per-step cost from O(n^3) to O(n^2 K), so 100% of instances finish inside 500 ms and the mean relative gap improves over pure nearest neighbor.

next_search_advice.direction: Vectorized O(n^2)-per-step farness+destionation-pull scoring: choose next city by argmax over unvisited u of (-a*d(cur,u) + b*mean_{v in U\u} d(u,v) + c*d(dest,u)), with candidate pruning to the K nearest unvisited to cur (K adaptive to n) to stay inside the 500 ms budget; evolve the coefficients (a,b,c,K) and the normalization (median/mean scaling) rather than adding deeper lookahead.
